1: As though some spell in sorrow bound him,
3: In sad expectance stood around him.
4: The lips of all had silence sealed,
5: Whilst, bent on him, each look observant,
6: Saw grief's deep trace and passion fervent
8: But the proud Khan his dark eye raising,
9: And on the courtiers fiercely gazing,
10: Gave signal to them to begone!
12: Now yields him to his bosom's smart,
14: Is traced the anguish of his heart;
15: As full fraught clouds on mirrors clear
17: What fills that haughty soul with pain?
18: What thoughts such madd'ning tumults cause?
19: With Russia plots he war again?
20: Would he to Poland dictate laws? Say, is the sword of vengeance glancing?
21: Does bold revolt claim nature's right?
23: Or sabres of fierce foes advancing?
24: Ah no! no more his proud steed prancing
25: Beneath him guides the Khan to war,--
26: Such thoughts his mind has banished far.
27: Has treason scaled the harem's wall,
28: Whose height might treason's self appal,
29: And slavery's daughter fled his power,
30: To yield her to the daring Giaour?
31: No! pining in his harem sadly,
32: No wife of his would act so madly;
33: To wish or think they scarcely dare;
34: By wretches, cold and heartless, guarded,
35: Hope from each breast so long discarded;
38: They bloom within the harem's towers,
39: As in a hot-house bloom the flowers
40: Which erst perfumed Arabia's field. To them the days in sameness dreary,
41: And months and years pass slow away,
42: In solitude, of life grown weary,
43: Well pleased they see their charms decay.
44: Each day, alas! the past resembling,
45: Time loiters through their halls and bowers;
46: In idleness, and fear, and trembling,
47: The captives pass their joyless hours.

52: Or by the noise of living streams,

62: His only law his chieftain's pleasure,

129: Who quits the world and all its woes,
130: To clasp thy charms within the harem,
131: Thou lovelier than the unplucked rose!
132: They sing, but-where, alas! is Zarem,
133: Love's star, the glory of the harem?
134: Pallid and sad no praise she hears,
135: Deaf to all sounds of joy her ears,
136: Downcast with grief, her youthful form
137: Yields like the palm tree to the storm,
138: Fair Zarem's dreams of bliss are o'er,
139: Her loved Giray loves her no more!
140: He leaves thee! yet whose charms divine Can equal, fair Grusinian! thine?
141: Shading thy brow, thy raven hair
142: Its lily fairness makes more fair;
143: Thine eyes of love appear more bright
144: Than noonday's beam, more dark than night;
145: Whose voice like thine can breathe of blisses,
146: Filling the heart with soft desire?
147: Like thine, ah! whose inflaming kisses
149: Who that has felt thy twining arms
150: Could quit them for another's charms?
151: Yet cold, and passionless, and cruel,
152: Giray can thy vast love despise,
153: Passing the lonesome night in sighs
155: Burns in his heart since the fair Pole
156: Is placed within the chief's control.
158: Had borne in conquest from afar;
160: Had gazed upon these foreign skies; Her aged father's boast and pride,
161: She bloomed in beauty by his side;
162: Each wish was granted ere expressed.
163: She to his heart the object dearest,
164: His sole desire to see her blessed;
165: As when the skies from clouds are clearest,
166: Still from her youthful heart to chase
168: Hoping in after life that never
171: But oft that fancy would retrace
172: Life's blissful spring-time decked in flowers.
173: Her form a thousand charms unfolded,
174: Her face by beauty's self was moulded,
175: Her dark blue eyes were full of fire,--
176: All nature's stores on her were lavished;
177: The magic harp with soft desire,
178: When touched by her, the senses ravished.
179: Warriors and knights had sought in vain
180: Maria's virgin heart to move, And many a youth in secret pain
181: Pined for her in despairing love.
182: But love she knew not, in her breast
183: Tranquil it had not yet intruded,
184: Her days in mirth, her nights in rest,
186: Passed heedless, peace her bosom's guest.

188: Rushed like a torrent o'er her nation,--
194: From their red ruins joy was banished,
199: In recent tomb her father lies;

212: His heart is at her grief afflicted,
214: And least of all Maria's will
215: Is by the harem's laws restricted.
216: The hateful guard, of all the dread,

223: The Khan to her such freedom gave;
227: It seemed as though some jewel rare,

232: The lamp of faith, incessant burning,
234: The comfort of the spirit mourning

278: Listens to hear the noise repeated,

280: Save where the fountains softly sounding

285: Luxurious East! how soft thy nights,
286: What magic through the soul they pour!
287: How fruitful they of fond delights
289: What splendour in each house is found,
293: When angry feelings cease to riot
294: There love inspires with softer sway!
296: The women sleep;--but one is there
297: Who sleeps not; goaded by despair
298: Her couch she quits with dread intent,
299: On awful errand is she bent;
300: Breathless she through the door swift flying
301: Passes unseen; her timid feet Scarce touch the floor, she glides so fleet.
303: The eunuch thwarts the fair one's path,
304: Ah! who can speak his bosom's wrath?
305: False is the quiet sleep would throw
306: Around that gray and care-worn brow;
307: She like a spirit vanished by
308: Viewless, unheard as her own sigh!
310: The door she reaches, trembling opes,
311: Enters, and looks around with awe,
313: Rushed through her heart at what she saw!
314: The image of the sacred maid,
316: And cross attracted first the fair,
317: By the dim lamp-light scarce displayed!
319: The vision burst upon thy soul,
320: The tongue long silent uttered praise,
321: The heart throbs high, but sin's control Cannot escape, 'tis passion, passion sways!

323: Slumbered, her cheek, tinged like the rose,
